packs.title: Skyline, Museums and Lake
packs.promise: Explore Chicago through its skyline, major museums, baseball and the lake.

q.s: Respond to an artist’s choices with a different composition.
st: Choose an accessible artwork and note artist and title.
Notice two shapes or colors.
Create an original composition using a different subject and arrangement.

q.s: Let a guided journey connect two buildings through a story.
st: Book a suitable sailing and follow the operator’s boarding directions.
During the cruise, compare two buildings discussed by the docent.
Afterward, record one sourced design fact and how your view changed.

q.s: Notice the lake between busier parts of the city.
st: Choose a comfortable permitted position clear of circulation.
Pause and notice one sound and one distant movement.
Write a short observation.

packs.title: Steel & Water
packs.promise: Find the small surprises inside a city of bold shapes.

q.s: Collect the small shapes that hold up a very tall street.
st: Begin at State and Washington. Choose either sidewalk and stay on that side for this short block.
Find three facade details: a repeating shape, a curve, and a change from one material to another. Door frames and lower windows count; looking high is optional.
Record each detail using a few words or a close composition that leaves people and shop interiors out.
Choose the detail you would normally have passed and explain what made it worth stopping for.

q.s: Make one straight building take an unexpected bend.
st: Approach Cloud Gate on an open park path. Find a clear position outside the busiest gathering area.
Choose one building visible both in the skyline and in the curved reflection. Watch how its edges change.
Make a two-part record: the building as it stands and the building as the reflection bends it. Two short descriptions work as well as photos.
Give the reflected version a new job, such as holding up a cloud, based on the shape you observed.

q.s: Let a winding bridge change the pace of your city day.
st: Find the BP Bridge entrance beside the east side of Jay Pritzker Pavilion. Check that the bridge is open before joining it.
Walk or roll at your own pace along the public route toward Maggie Daley Park. You may turn back whenever you have enough observations.
Notice one thing the curve hides and then reveals, plus one change in the nearby city sound or visible movement.
At a clear stopping place off the through-route, record what changed between the two parks and choose a word for your new pace.
